verses.sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              धार्मिकोऽर्थानसम्प्राप्य राजामात्यैः प्रबाधितः। च्युतः कोशाच्च दण्डाच्च सुखमिच्छन्कथं चरेत्॥१॥
verses.english: Yudhishthira said Time, which is a terror to all creatures, is rolling on. What is that source of good for which one should try? Tell me this, O grandfather.

verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              अत्रायं क्षेमदर्शीय इतिहासोऽनुगीयते। तत्तेऽहं सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि तन्निबोध युधिष्ठिर॥२॥
verses.english: Bhishma said Regarding it is cited the old discourse between father and son. Listen to it, 0 Yudhishthira.

verses.sanskrit: क्षेमदर्शी नृपसुतो यत्र क्षीणबलः पुरा। मुनिं कालकवृक्षीयमाजगामेति नः श्रुतम्। तं पप्रच्छानुसंगृह्य कृच्छ्रामापदमास्थितः॥३॥
verses.english: Once on a time, O son of Pritha, a twiceborn person devoted to only the study of the Vedas had a very intelligent son who passed by the name of Medhavin.

verses.sanskrit: राजोवाच। अर्थेषु भागी पुरुष ईहमानः पुनः पुनः। अलब्ध्वा मद्विधो राज्यं ब्रह्मन्किं कर्तुमर्हति॥४॥
verses.english: Himself a master of the religion of Liberation, the son one day asked his father who was not conversant with that religion and who was engaged in following the Vedic precepts, this question.

verses.sanskrit: अन्यत्र मरणाद्दैन्यादन्यत्र परसंश्रयात्। क्षुद्रादन्यत्र चाचारात्तन्ममाचक्ष्व सत्तम॥५॥
व्याधिना चाभिपन्नस्य मानसेनेतरेण वा। धर्मज्ञश्च कृतज्ञश्च त्वद्विधः शरणं भवेत्॥६॥
निर्विद्यति नरः कामान्निर्विद्य सुखमेधते। त्यक्त्वा प्रीतिं च शोकं च लब्ध्वा बुद्धिमयं वसु॥७॥
सुखमर्थाश्रयं येषामनुशोचामि तानहम्। मम ह्यर्थाः सुबहवो नष्टाः स्वप्न इवागताः॥८॥
दुष्करं बत कुर्वन्ति महतोऽर्थांस्त्यिजन्ति ये। वयं त्वेतान्परित्यक्तुमसतोऽपि न शक्नुमः॥९॥
verses.english: The sire said How is the world attacked?-By what is it besieged? What are those irresistible things that are falling on all sides? Do you frighten me with your words?-

verses.sanskrit: इमामवस्थां सम्प्राप्तं दीनमार्तं श्रिया च्युतम्। यदन्यत्सुखमस्तीह तद्ब्रह्मन्ननुशाधि माम्॥१०॥
कौसल्येनैवमुक्तस्तु राजपुत्रेण धीमता। मुनिः कालकवृक्षीयः प्रत्युवाच महाद्युतिः॥११॥
मुनिरुवाच। पुरस्तादेव ते बुद्धिरियं कार्या विजानता। अनित्यं सर्वमेवैतदहं च मम चास्ति यत्॥१२॥
verses.english: When with every night the period of a man's existence wears away, when, indeed, one's position is similar to that of a fish a pool of shallow water, who can be happy?

verses.sanskrit: यत्किंचिन्मन्यसेऽस्तीति सर्वं नास्तीति विद्धि तत्। एवं न व्यथते प्राज्ञः कृच्छ्रामप्यापदं गतः॥१३॥
यद्धि भूतं भविष्यं च सर्वं तन्न भविष्यति। एवं विदितवेद्यस्त्वमधर्मेभ्यः प्रमोक्ष्यसे॥१४॥
verses.english: What is kept for being done tomorrow should be done to-day; and what one thinks of doing in the afternoon should be done in the forenoon. Death does not wait for a man whether he has, or has not done his acts.

verses.sanskrit: यच्च पूर्वं समाहारे यच्च पूर्वं परे परे। सर्वं तन्नास्ति ते चैव तज्ज्ञात्वा कोऽनुसंज्वरेत्॥१५॥
भूत्वा च न भवत्येतदभूत्वा च भविष्यति। शोके न ह्यस्ति सामर्थ्यं शोकं कुर्यात्कथंचन॥१६॥
क्व नु तेऽद्य पिता राजन् क्व नु तेऽद्य पितामहः। न त्वं पश्यसि तानद्य न त्वां पश्यन्ति तेऽपि च॥१७॥
verses.english: Where, O king, is your father, to-day and where your grandfathers? You do not see them to-day and they do not see you. O sinless one.

verses.sanskrit: आत्मनोऽध्रुवतां पश्यंस्तांस्त्वं किमनुशोचसि। बुद्ध्या चैवानुबुद्ध्यस्व ध्रुवं हि न भविष्यसि॥१८॥
verses.english: By performing deeds good or bad, one pleases his people. Death seizes him possessed of sons and animals, and with mind given to them, and runs away like a tiger carrying away a sleeping deer. While still engaged in acquiring various objects of desire, and while still unsatiated with their enjoyment, Death attacks him and runs away like a she-wolf seizing a sheep and running away with it.-_'This has been done,-this remain to be done this other is half done'-one may say thus, but Death, not caring for a person's desire to finish his unfinished acts, seizes and drags him away. Death seizes and carries away one who has not yet gained the fruit of what he has already done, amongst those attached to action, one busied with his field or shop or house. Death seizes and carries away the weak, the strong, the wise, the brave, the idiotic, the learned, or him who has not yet obtained the gratification of any of his desires. Death, decrepitude, disease, sorrow, and many things of a similar nature, cannot he shunned by mortals. How then O father, can you sit so at your ease? As soon as an embodied creature is born, Decrepitude and Death come and possess him for his destruction.

verses.sanskrit: अहं च त्वं च नृपते सुहृदः शत्रवश्च ते। अवश्यं न भविष्यामः सर्वं च न भविष्यति॥१९॥
verses.english: All forms of existence, mobile and immobile, are possessed by these two. When the soldiers, which constitute Death's army, march, nothing can resist them except that one thing, viz., the power of Truth, for in Truth alone Immortality lives. The joy which one feels of living in the midst of men is residence of Death.

verses.sanskrit: ये तु विंशतिवर्षा वै त्रिंशद्वर्षाश्च मानवाः। अर्वागेव हि ते सर्वे मरिष्यन्ति शरच्छतात्॥२०॥
verses.english: The Shruti says that what is called the forest is the true fold for the deities, while the joy one feels in living in the midst of men is, as it were, the fetter for binding the dweller.

verses.sanskrit: अपि चेन्महतो वित्तान्न प्रमुच्येत पूरुषः। नैतन्ममेति तन्मत्वा कुर्वीत प्रियमात्मनः॥२१॥
verses.english: The pious cut it and escape. The sinful can not cut it. He who does not injure other creatures in thought, word, and deed, and who never injures others by taking away their means of livelihood, is never injured by any crcature. Therefore, one should practise the vow of truth, be steadfastly devoted to the vow of truth, and should wish for nothing but the truth. Governing all his senses and regarding all creatures impartially, one should defeat Death with the help of Truth. Both Immortality and Death are in the body.

verses.sanskrit: अनागतं यन्न ममेति विद्यादतिक्रान्तं यन्न ममेति विद्यात्। दिष्टं बलीय इति मन्यमानास्ते पण्डितास्तत्सतां स्थानमाहुः॥२२॥
verses.english: Death comes from folly, and Immortality is acquired by Truth. Transcending desire and anger, abstaining from injury, I shall adopt Truth and happily acquiring what is for my behoof avoid Death like an Immortal. Engaged in the Sacrifice that is formed by Peace, and employed also in the Sacrifice of Brahma, and controlling my senses, the Sacrifices I shall perform and those of speech, mind, and deeds, when the sun enters his northerly course. How can one like me celebrate an Animal Sacrifice which is full of cruelty.

verses.sanskrit: अनाढ्याश्चापि जीवन्ति राज्यं चाप्यनुशासति। बुद्धिपौरुषसम्पन्नास्त्वया तुल्याधिका जनाः॥२३॥
verses.english: How can one like me, endued with wisdom, perform like a cruel being, a Sacrifice of destruction after the manner of what is sanctioned for the Kshatriyas,-a Sacrifice which produces only fickle rewards, In myself have I been begotten by myown self. O father, without seeking to procreate progeny, I shall rest myself on my own self!

verses.sanskrit: न च त्वमिव शोचन्ति तस्मात्त्वमपि मा शुचः। किं न त्वं तैर्नरैः श्रेयांस्तुल्यो वा बुद्धिपौरुषैः॥२४॥
verses.english: I shall celebrate the Sacrifice of Self, I require no children to rescue me. He whose words and thoughts are always well-governed, he who has penances and Renunciation, and Yoga, is sure to acquire everything through these. There is no eye like Knowledge. There is no reward like Knowledge. There is no sorrow like attachment. There is no happiness like Renunciation.

verses.sanskrit: राजोवाच। यादृच्छिकं सर्वमासीत्तद्राज्यमिति चिन्तये। ह्रियते सर्वमेवेदं कालेन महता द्विज॥२५॥
verses.english: For a Brahmana there can be no wealth like living in solitude, an impartial eye for all creatures, truthfulness of speech, steady observance of good conduct, the total abandonment of the rod (of chastisement), simplicity, and the gradual abstention from all acts.

verses.sanskrit: तस्यैव ह्रियमाणस्य स्त्रोतसेव तपोधन। फलमेतत्प्रपश्यामि यथालब्धेन वर्तयन्॥२६॥
verses.english: Why do you require riches, relatives, friends, and wives? You are a Brahmana and you have death to encounter! Search you own Self which is concealed in a cave. Where have your grandfathers gone and where your father too?

verses.sanskrit: मुनिरुवाच। अनागतमतीतं च याथातथ्यविनिश्चयात्। नानुशोचेत कौसल्य सर्वार्थेषु तथा भव॥२७॥
verses.english: Bhishma said, Hearing these words of his son, the father acted in the way that was pointed out, O king! Do you also act similarly, devoted to the religion of Truth.

verses.sanskrit: अवाप्यान्कामयन्नर्थान्नानवाप्यान्कदाचन। प्रत्युत्पन्नाननुभवन्मा शुचस्त्वमनागतान्॥२८॥
verses.english: Bhishma said, Hearing these words of his son, the father acted in the way that was pointed out, O king! Do you also act similarly, devoted to the religion of Truth.

verses.sanskrit: यथा लब्धोपपन्नार्थैस्तथा कौसल्य रंस्यसे। कच्चिच्छुद्धस्वभावेन श्रिया हीनो न शोचसि॥२९॥
verses.english: Be you satisfied, O prince of Koshala, with whatever you can easily get. Even if divested of prosperity, do not grieve for it but try to maintain a pure character.

verses.sanskrit: पुरस्ताद्भूतपूर्वत्वाद्धीनभाग्यो हि दुर्मतिः। धातारं गर्हते नित्यं लब्धार्थश्च न मृष्यते॥३०॥
verses.english: Only an unfortunate and foolish wight when divested of former prosperity, blames the supreme Ordainer, without being contented with his present position.

verses.sanskrit: अनर्हानपि चैवान्यान्मन्यते श्रीमतो जनान्। एतस्मात्कारणादेतद्दुःखं भूयोऽनुवर्तते॥३१॥
verses.english: Such a person consider others however undeserving, as men blessed with prosperity. Therefore, those who are possessed of malice and vanity and puffed up with a sense of egoism, suffer more misery still. You however, O king, are not sullied by such vices.

verses.sanskrit: ईर्ष्याभिमानसम्पन्ना राजन्पुरुषमानिनः। कच्चित्त्वं न तथा राजन्मत्सरी कोसलाधिप॥३२॥
सहस्व श्रियमन्येषां यद्यपि त्वयि नास्ति सा। अन्यत्रापि सतीं लक्ष्मीं कुशला भुञ्जते सदा॥३३॥
verses.english: Bear the prosperity of others, inspite of your being divested of the same. Clever and expert men succeed in enjoying the prosperity of their enemies.

verses.sanskrit: श्रियं च पुत्रपौत्रं च मनुष्या धर्मचारिणः। योगधर्मविदो धीराः स्वयमेव त्यजन्त्युत॥३४॥
verses.english: Prosperity relinquishes the person that hates others. Pious and wise men conversant with the duties of Yoga renounce prosperity and sons and grandsons of their own accord.

verses.sanskrit: बहुसंकुसुकं दृष्ट्वा विधित्सासाधनेन च। तथाऽन्ये संत्यजन्त्येव मत्वा परमदुर्लभम्॥३५॥
verses.english: Others, considering earthly possessions to be exceedingly unstable and unobtainable, and dependent upon continued exertion, are also scen to renounce it.

verses.sanskrit: त्त्वं पुनः प्राज्ञरूपः सन् कृपणं परितप्यसे। अकाम्यान्कामयानोऽर्थान् पराधीनानुपद्रवान्॥३६॥
verses.english: You seem to be endued with wisdom. Why, then, do you grieve so piteously, seeking for things which should not be sought for, since they are unstable and dependent on others?

verses.sanskrit: तां बुद्धिमुपजिज्ञासुस्त्वमेवैतान्परित्यज। अनर्थाश्चार्थरूपेण ह्यर्थाश्चानर्थरूपिणः॥३७॥
verses.english: You wish to know the temperament of mind which would give you happiness. The advice I give you is to renounce all objects of desire! Objects which should be discarded appear to one as those which he should seek to secure, while those which should be secured appear to him as objects which should be avoided.

verses.sanskrit: अर्थायैव हि केषांचिद्धननाशो भवत्युत। आनन्त्यं तत्सुखं मत्वा श्रियमन्यः परीप्सति॥३८॥
verses.english: Some loss their wealth while seeking the same. Others consider wealth, as the source of endless happiness, and, therefore pursue it eagerly.

verses.sanskrit: रममाणः श्रिया कश्चिन्नान्यच्छ्रेयोऽभिमन्यते। तथा तस्येहमानस्य समारम्भो विनश्यति॥३९॥
verses.english: Some again, overjoyed with wealth, think that there is nothing superior to it. While cagerly seeking for the acquisition of wealth, such a person loses all other objects of life. renounce

verses.sanskrit: कृच्छ्राल्लब्धमभिप्रेतं यदि कौसल्य नश्यति। तदा निर्विद्यते सोऽर्थात्परिभग्नक्रमो नरः॥४०॥
verses.english: If, O prince of Koshala, a person loses that wealth which had been acquired with difficulty and after which he had hankered, he then, overcome by despair, gives up all desire of wealth.

verses.sanskrit: धर्ममेकेऽभिपद्यन्ते कल्याणाभिजना नराः। परत्र सुखमिच्छन्तो निर्विद्येयुश्च लौकिकात्॥४१॥
verses.english: Some righteous and highly-born persons devote themselves to the acquisitions of virtue. These every king of worldly happiness from securing the same in the other world.

verses.sanskrit: जीवितं संत्यजन्त्येके धनलोभपरा जनाः। न जीवितार्थं मन्यन्ते पुरुषा हि धनादृते॥४२॥
verses.english: Some persons sacrifice life itself, actuated by the desire of acquiring wealth. These do not think that life without wealth has any use.

verses.sanskrit: पश्य तेषां कृपणतां पश्य तेषामबुद्धिताम्। अध्रुवे जीविते मोहादर्थदृष्टिमुपाश्रिताः॥४३॥
verses.english: Mark at their pitiable condition! Witness their foolishness! When life is so short and uncertain, these men, actuated by ignorance, seek wealth.

verses.sanskrit: संचये च विनाशान्ते मरणान्ते च जीवित। संयोगे च वियोगान्ते को नु विप्रणयेन्मनः॥४४॥
verses.english: Who is there that would busy himself with boarding when destruction is its end, hanker after life when death is its end, and after union when separation is its end?

verses.sanskrit: धनं वा पुरुषो राजन्पुरुषं वा पुनर्धनम्। अवश्यं प्रजहात्येव तद्विद्वान्कोऽनुसंज्वरेत्॥४५॥
verses.english: Sometimes man renounces wealth, and sometimes wealth renounces man. What man endued with knowledge is there who would grieve at the loss of wealth? There are many other persons in the world who lose wealth and friends.

verses.sanskrit: अन्येषामपि नश्यन्ति सुहृदश्च धनानि च। पश्य बुद्ध्या मनुष्याणां राजन्नापदमात्मनः॥४६॥
verses.english: See, O king, with your intelligence, and you will come to learn that the calamities which befall men are all owing to their own conduct! Do you, therefore, control your senses, mind and speech.

verses.sanskrit: नियच्छ यच्छ संयच्छ इन्द्रियाणि मनो गिरम्। प्रतिषेद्धा न चाप्येषु दुर्बलेष्वहितेष्वपि। प्राप्तिसृष्टेषु भावेषु व्यपकृष्टेष्वसम्भवे॥४७॥
verses.english: For, if these become weak and productive of evil there is no man who can stand aloof from temptation of external objects by which he is always surrounded. As no one can from a good idea of the past nor of the future, there being many intervals of time and place, a person like you who are endued with such wisdom and such prowess, never grieve for union and separation, for good or evil.

verses.sanskrit: प्रज्ञानतृप्तो विक्रान्तस्त्वद्विधो नानुशोचति। अल्पमिच्छन्नचपलो मृदुर्दान्तः सुनिश्चितः। ब्रह्मचर्योपपन्नश्च त्वद्विधो नैव शोचति॥४९॥
verses.english: A person so mild by nature, of controlled self, and settled conclusions, and observant of Brahmacharya vows, never grieve and never becomes restless from the desire of acquiring from the fear of losing anything insignificant.

verses.sanskrit: न त्वेव जाल्मीं कापालीं वृत्तिमेषितुमर्हसि। नृशंसवृत्तिं पापिष्ठां दुष्टां कापुरुषोचिताम्॥५०॥
verses.english: It is not proper that such a man should follow a deceitful life of mendicancy, a life that is sinful and wicked and cruel and which benefits only a human wretch.

verses.sanskrit: अपि मूलफलाजीवो रमस्वैको महावने। वाग्यत संगृहीतात्मा सर्वभूतदयान्वितः॥५१॥
verses.english: Do you go to the great forest and lead a life of happiness there, all alone and subsisting upon fruits and roots, restraining words and soul, and filled with mercy for all creatures.

verses.sanskrit: सदृशं पण्डितस्यैतदीषादन्तेन दन्तिना। यदेको रमतेऽरण्येष्वारण्येनैव तुष्यति॥५२॥
verses.english: Or He, who cheerfully leads such a life in the forest, having elephants of large tusks for companions, with no human being by his side, and contented with the produce of the forest, is said to follow the footsteps of the wise.

verses.sanskrit: महाह्रदः संक्षुभित आत्मनैव प्रसीदति। एतदेवं गतस्याहं सुखं पश्यामि जीवितुम्॥५३॥
verses.english: A large lake, when it becomes disturbed, becomes silent itself. Likewise, a wise men, when disturbed in such matters, becomes tranquil of himself. I see that a person, who has been reduced to such a plight as yours, may live happily even thus.

verses.sanskrit: असम्भवे श्रियो राजन्हीनस्य सचिवादिभिः। दैवे प्रतिनिविष्टे च किं श्रेयो मन्यते भवान्॥५४॥
verses.english: When it is impossible for you to recover your prosperity and when you are without ministers and counsellors, such a course is open to you. Do you expect to reap any benefit by depending upon destiny?
